client_spec.name: Default targets (replace with the client's spec)

nodes.label: RF Freq (13.56/27 MHz)
nodes.equation: n_e ∝ ω^(1.3–2.0),   V_sh ∝ ω^(-1) to ω^(-2)  (at fixed P_RF)
nodes.summary: Primary electrodynamic knob decoupling bulk electron dissociation density from collisional sheath ion bombardment energy.
nodes.failure_mode: 13.56 MHz alone sustains higher V_sh (risking mouth cusping at low P); 27.12 MHz narrows bimodal IEDF ΔE but accelerates C2H- nucleation if Ar residence sweep is slow.

nodes.label: RF Power (1.2-2.0 kW)
nodes.summary: Drives electron-impact dissociation of C2H2 (5.7–7.5 eV) and NH3 (4.5 eV) and controls sheath voltage amplitude.
nodes.failure_mode: Above ~1850 W at narrow gap (<=415 mils), high sheath electric fields amplify 3ω harmonics, increase RMS roughness >3.5x, and accelerate nanoparticle concentration.

nodes.label: Gap (400-500 mils)
nodes.equation: τ_res = (π R² d · P) / (Q_std · P_0) · (T_0 / T_g),   ΔP_Pois = 3 μ Q / (π d³)
nodes.summary: Showerhead-to-pedestal spacing governing gas residence time τ_res, bulk-to-sheath volume ratio, Poiseuille radial drop, and (p_eff·d, f·d) similarity coordinates.
nodes.failure_mode: Wide gap (>500 mils) prolongs τ_res past τ_nuc (gas-phase soot); ultra-narrow micro-gaps (<1 mm) choke Poiseuille radial flow or overlap RF sheaths (2 s_m / d -> 1).

nodes.label: Pressure (14-22 Torr)
nodes.summary: High-pressure regime collisionalizes the RF sheath (30–60 ion-neutral collisions, thermalizing angled ions) while keeping feature transport strictly ballistic (Kn ≈ 60–140).
nodes.failure_mode: Above ~20.3 Torr at low Ar flow, Langevin C2nH- chain polymerization drops τ_nuc ~ P^(-2.15) while lengthening τ_res ~ P, nucleating killer surface nodules (Coupon A29-2).

nodes.label: Ar Flow (7-12 slm)
nodes.equation: τ_res ∝ 1 / Q_total,   Ar_m(11.55 eV) + C2H2 -> C2H• + H• + Ar
nodes.summary: High-velocity convective carrier sweep that flushes C2nH- negative-ion nuclei out of the gap before agglomeration and supplies clean Ar+ / Ar* Penning dissociation.
nodes.failure_mode: Low Ar (<8.5 slm at >19 Torr, Slide-2 Ar 7k grid) allows polyyne oligomer stagnation and steep high-pressure overburden spikes.

nodes.label: C₂H₂ (600-700 sccm)
nodes.summary: Triple-bonded sp-hybridized carbon precursor delivering high sp² skeletal carbon density and fast deposition rate, while cooling bulk T_e via vibrational excitation.
nodes.failure_mode: Excess C2H2 relative to NH3 yields unpassivated ethynyl C2H• radicals (β_0 ~ 0.5) and C2H- anions (~30% electronegativity), pinching off deep keyhole voids.

nodes.label: NH₃ (150-250 sccm)
nodes.equation: C2Hx + NHx• -> HCN(g)↑ + H2  |  -C* + H•/NHx• -> -C-H / -C-NH2
nodes.summary: Quadruple-action modifier: (1) scavenges excess C into volatile HCN(g), (2) passivates dangling bonds to drop β_eff, (3) drives top-field H/NHx scour, (4) relieves ring strain & boosts F-barrier to 4.92 eV.
nodes.failure_mode: Too low (<175 sccm): mouth bread-loafing + dust nodules. Too high (N/C > 0.43): terminal nitrile -C≡N (2150 cm⁻¹) breaks sp² crosslinking and lowers density <1.70 g/cm³.

nodes.label: Temp (530-580 °C)
nodes.equation: sp³-CHx --(Δ)--> sp²-C=C + H2(g)↑,   n_g = P / (k_B T_g)
nodes.summary: Drives in-situ H2 effusion for zero post-cure shrinkage, dense sp² crosslinking (>1.80 g/cm³), thermally activated H/NHx top-field etching, and exponential boundary-layer τ_nuc dust delay.
nodes.failure_mode: Above ~572 °C with low NH3 (<190 sccm), thermal recombinative H2 desorption strips -C-H passivation, causing β_eff to rebound at feature entrances.

nodes.label: Plasma n_e & T_e
nodes.equation: R_diss = k_diss(T_e) n_e n_g + k_Penning [Ar_m][C2H2]
nodes.summary: Bulk electron density and C2H2-cooled electron energy distribution driving volumetric cracking of NH3 into passivating H•/NHx• and C2H2 into ethynyl precursors.
nodes.failure_mode: Over-dissociation without convective Ar sweep floods the plasma core with sticky C2H• and C4H2 diacetylene oligomers.

nodes.label: Sheath V_sh & E_i
nodes.equation: E_i ≈ e V_sh / (1 + s_m / λ_i),   E_th,Ar = 16 eV << E_th,CF4 = 156 eV
nodes.summary: Mean kinetic energy of clean Ar+/NHx+ ions crossing 30–60 charge-exchange collisions; arrives near 0° normal incidence on the horizontal top field and feature floor.
nodes.failure_mode: High E_i (>35 eV) deflects ions onto upper sidewalls (creating active dangling sites & cusps) and elevates compressive stress; <10 eV starves Steinbrüchel planar trim.

nodes.label: H•/NHx• & HCN Scav.
nodes.equation: Γ_(H+NHx) / Γ_(C2Hx)   &   C2Hx + NHx• -> HCN(g)↑ + H2(g)
nodes.summary: Coupled ratio of passivating/etching hydrogen-amino radicals and gas-phase HCN volatile carbon removal relative to raw hydrocarbon deposition flux.
nodes.failure_mode: Weak HCN scavenging leaves polyyne clusters in the boundary layer, thickening planar overburden and choking 110 nm hole throats.

nodes.label: Dust Margin τ_nuc/τ_res
nodes.equation: η_dust = τ_nuc(P, T_g, N/C, P_RF) / τ_res(P, d, Q_Ar, T_g),   C_{2n}H⁻ + C2H2 -> C_{2n+2}H⁻
nodes.summary: Dimensionless safety margin comparing electrostatic C2nH- nanoparticle nucleation induction time against convective reactor sweep time.
nodes.failure_mode: When η_dust < 1.1, trapped C12H- cores grow into 50–180 nm negatively charged carbon spheres (Z_p ~ 130e), falling onto the wafer as killer surface nodules (Coupon A29-2).

nodes.label: OES (CN/Ar, Hα/C₂)
nodes.summary: Non-invasive optical emission ratios tracking volatile HCN carbon scavenging (CN 388 nm), atomic H passivation (Hα 656.5 nm), and C2 Swan (515.9 nm) polyyne clustering against Ar 750.4 nm.
nodes.failure_mode: Rising I(C2 516)/I(CH 430) with falling I(CN 388)/I(Ar 750) signals imminent gas-phase polyyne oligomerization and mouth pinch-off before wafer cleavage.

nodes.label: RF V_dc & 3ω/1ω
nodes.equation: I_RF(t) = C_sh(V(t)) dV/dt  =>  |I_3ω / I_1ω| ↑ with nonlinear sheath & α = n_-/n_e
nodes.summary: Inline V-I probe harmonic FFT and DC self-bias telemetry diagnosing nonlinear RF sheath capacitance modulation, electronegative C2nH- core trapping, and narrow-gap micro-arcing.
nodes.failure_mode: Sudden |V_dc| collapse + I_3ω/I_1ω spike (>11%) indicates bulk electron depletion onto growing negative carbon nanoparticles (Z_p δ >> 1).

nodes.label: Mobility (1/β_eff)
nodes.equation: β_eff = β_C0 exp(-k_pass θ_(H/NHx)),   Φ_hole² = 3 AR² β_eff vs Φ_trench² = 1 AR² β_eff (what-if ratio 2–4)
nodes.summary: Inverse effective sticking probability inside free-molecular HAR holes (λ_n ≈ 7–15 µm >> D = 110 nm); sets how many ballistic wall collisions a precursor survives to reach z = 1.0 µm.
nodes.failure_mode: High sticking (β_eff > 0.025) drives circular-hole Thiele modulus Φ_hole > 2.5 (2–4x higher Φ² than 2D trenches), depositing carbon at the entrance and pinching off a keyhole void.

nodes.label: Top-Field Etch Diff.
nodes.equation: v_net(z) = v_dep,0 Γ̃_C(z)(1 - θ_pass(z)) - Y_chem Γ_E(z) - b_Ar(√E_i - √16) Γ_i F_view(z)
nodes.summary: Solid-angle view-factor + sidewall recombination differential: exposed top field (Ω = 2π) undergoes rapid H•/NHx• + Ar+ Steinbrüchel trim while shadowed deep interiors accumulate carbon.
nodes.failure_mode: Weak top-etch differential leaves thick planar overburden (>180 nm) and fails to shave nascent upper-corner bread-loafing cusps.

nodes.label: a-C:H:N Stress & ρ
nodes.summary: Amorphous carbon-nitride network combining 550 °C H2-desorbed sp² crosslinking (zero shrinkage, E_th,CF4 = 156 eV) with 3–8 at.% trivalent C=N ring-strain relief and 4.92 eV fluorine diffusion barrier.
nodes.failure_mode: Undoped high compressive stress (>380 MPa) causes collar delamination cracks; over-doping (N/C > 0.43) creates terminal -C≡N chains that soften film density.

nodes.label: PH Depth (1000=Seamless)
nodes.equation: SC_geom = sech(√(C_geom AR² β_eff)) · Boost_inhibitor,   h*(t) = ∫ v_net(z=L) dt
nodes.summary: Carbon plug penetration depth from the mouth (plug mode) or bottom-up fill height h* (partial mode) inside 1.0 µm deep tapered HAR holes (110 nm AR=9.1 & 225 nm AR=4.4).
nodes.failure_mode: Collar bread-loafing pinch-off at PH = 635–770 nm (Slide-1 A28-2, A29-2, A30-2) traps an inverted-teardrop keyhole void (28–36 nm max width) that causes etch punch-through.

nodes.label: Overburden & AFM Rq (nm)
nodes.window: Plug < 85–125 nm | Partial < 45 nm | AFM Rq < 2.0 nm
nodes.equation: t_OB = ∫ v_net(z=0) dt · (1 - α_trim f_trim),   Δh_dual-CD = |t_OB(110) - t_OB(225)|,   Rq(N/C, P_RF, T_s)
nodes.summary: Curved carbon overburden cap, dual-CD array recess dimple Δh_step, and non-destructive inline AFM RMS roughness Rq governing etch-back budget and SEM thickness CI.
nodes.failure_mode: OB > 155–253 nm (Slide-1 A29-2 & A30-2) or rough mounded cap (Rq > 3 nm) drives strain energy G past interfacial toughness G_c, triggering overburden delamination.

nodes.label: Crack & Nodule Risk
nodes.window: Spec: Crack = No, Nodule = None (<10% risk)
nodes.equation: G_strain = (σ_comp² · t_OB) / (2 E') < G_c   &   η_dust ≥ 1.5
nodes.summary: Joint defect probability combining Griffith compressive-strain overburden delamination cracking and hemispherical gas-phase nanoparticle nodule incorporation.
nodes.failure_mode: Any delamination crack ('Crack: Yes' on A28-2..A30-2) or >40 nm spherical dust nodule bump ('A29-2') causes immediate pattern collapse or lithography focus failure.

edges.mechanism: Doubling excitation from 13.56 to 27.12 MHz enhances sheath-edge electron heating, boosting bulk electron density n_e and radical dissociation by ~2–3x at fixed RF power.
Higher displacement current C·dV/dt at 27.12 MHz requires a much smaller RF sheath voltage V_sh for the same power, dropping collisional ion impact energy E_i.
Higher RF power directly increases absorbed electron power density, raising n_e and dissociation rates of C2H2 and NH3.
Higher RF power expands RF voltage amplitude and DC self-bias |V_dc|, increasing ion acceleration across the collisional sheath.
Wider inter-electrode spacing increases active chamber volume V = πR²d and gas residence time τ_res, giving C2nH- anions more time to nucleate dust.
At 14–22 Torr, ion-neutral charge-exchange mean free path (~10 µm) is ~40x thinner than the sheath, thermalizing ion energy and eliminating overhang sputtering.
Higher pressure simultaneously lengthens residence time τ_res ∝ P and accelerates C2H- + C2H2 chain polymerization (τ_nuc ∝ P^-2.15).
High Ar flow (8–12 slm) convectively sweeps negatively charged C2nH- clusters out of the gap before they reach critical agglomeration size.
Higher C2H2 partial pressure accelerates dissociative attachment (e- + C2H2 -> C2H- + H) and consecutive polyyne chain insertion.
Higher C2H2 supply directly increases net hydrocarbon radical flux Γ_C2Hx landing on the exposed horizontal field.
NH3 dissociation supplies H•, NH•, and NH2• radicals that passivate surface dangling bonds and convert excess C2Hx oligomers into volatile HCN gas.
Incorporating 3–8 at.% trivalent nitrogen (C=N / C-N) terminates over-constrained carbon rings, relieving intrinsic compressive film stress.
Heating the wafer to 530–580 °C rarefies gas density n_g = P/(k_B T_g) and exponentially delays carbon nanoparticle nucleation time τ_nuc.
High substrate temperature thermally activates chemical etching of weak sp³-CHx polymeric carbon by atomic H• and NHx• radicals.
Above 530 °C, in-situ H2 desorption relaxes strained C-H cages into a dense, thermally stable, zero-shrinkage sp²-crosslinked carbon network.
Higher electron density cracks N-H bonds (4.5 eV) in NH3 to generate abundant atomic H• and amino radicals.
Surface -H/-NHx termination caps dangling carbon radicals, dropping effective sticking coefficient β_eff by >10x so precursors bounce deep into AR=9 holes.
High H•/NHx• flux scours horizontal field and upper hole corners where plasma solid-angle view factor is wide, while recombining along sidewalls.
Volatile HCN formation chemically peels carbon out of growing hydrocarbon clusters, shrinking both nanoparticle size and concentration.
Low-to-moderate directional Ar+/NHx+ ions strike the flat planar field at 0° incidence, driving ion-enhanced chemical etching of top overburden.
Energetic ion bombardment creates dangling-bond active sites near feature entrances, locally increasing precursor sticking probability.
High radical mobility (low β_eff) lowers the Knudsen Thiele modulus Φ_hole, allowing carbon precursors to fill all the way to 1000 nm without mouth pinch-off.
edges.scaling_law: PH Depth -> 1000 nm as Φ_hole = √(6 AR² β_eff) < 1

edges.mechanism: Shaving nascent top-corner overhang keeps the 100–120 nm hole throat open until bottom-up / superconformal closure completes.
Selective chemical/ion-assisted etching on the exposed planar field directly suppresses net planar overburden accumulation.
Maintaining η_dust = τ_nuc/τ_res > 1.4 prevents gas-phase particle inclusions that nucleate surface nodules and stress-concentration cracks.
Strain energy release rate G = σ²·t_OB/(2E') scales linearly with overburden thickness: coupons A29-2 (253 nm) & A30-2 (203 nm) crack heavily above ~155 nm OB.
High unrelieved intrinsic stress drives film delamination and collar micro-cracking at the sharp 90° top corners of HAR hole arrays.
VHF 27.12 MHz lowers V_sh (preventing mouth cusping) while N/C in 0.31-0.41 passivates sites (β_eff < 0.01) & scavenges C2Hx into HCN.
edges.scaling_law: Human Rule (HR-03): if freq_mhz > 20 and nc_ratio >= 0.31 and nc_ratio <= 0.41

edges.mechanism: At Gap <= 415 mils and Power >= 1850 W, high sheath electric field triggers localized micro-arcing and rough overburden.
edges.scaling_law: Human Rule (HR-04): if gap_mils <= 415 and power_w >= 1850

edges.mechanism: Above 572 °C with low NH3 (<190 sccm), rapid H2 desorption re-opens dangling carbon sites, raising β_eff at hole mouths.
edges.scaling_law: Human Rule (HR-05): if temp_c > 572 and nh3_sccm < 190

edges.mechanism: Higher RF power raises C2H• and C2H- seed radical density, shortening nanoparticle induction time τ_nuc.
Wider inter-electrode spacing raises p_eff·d similarity product and lowers sheath electric field E = V_RF / d, moderately reducing E_i.
Argon dilution (>90%) sustains higher bulk T_e and supplies 11.55 eV Ar_m metastables that Penning-dissociate C2H2 while keeping Ar+ as the clean sheath ion.
Electron impact populates Ar(4p) (750.4 nm, E_th=14.24 eV), Hα (656.5 nm), CH (430.3 nm), C2 (515.9 nm), and CN (388.3 nm) radiative states.
Active HCN volatile scavenging raises CN 388.3 nm / Ar 750.4 nm and Hα 656.5 nm / C2 515.9 nm emission ratios while suppressing C2 Swan polyyne bands.
Larger RF sheath voltage swing increases DC self-bias |V_dc| and nonlinear space-charge sheath harmonic generation (2ω, 3ω).
When dust margin η drops, growing nanoparticles acquire Z_p ~ 13–268e negative charge (α = Z_p n_p/n_e >> 1), depleting free bulk electrons and distorting I_3ω/I_1ω.
High inline I(CN 388)/I(Ar 750) and I(Hα 656)/I(C2 516) directly observe passivating radical dominance over unpassivated C2/C2H clustering.
edges.scaling_law: Virtual metrology anchor for θ_passiv & β_eff

edges.mechanism: Elevated |V_dc| and sheath harmonic distortion track energetic ion subplantation and high-power surface roughening / compressive stress buildup.
Higher sheath ion bombardment energy densifies the film via knock-on subplantation but increases intrinsic compressive stress |σ_comp|.
Suppressing boundary-layer polyyne oligomer condensation prevents the +90–150 nm rough overburden spike observed on high-P low-Ar Coupon A29-2 (253–370 nm).

reaction_network.role: Generates metastable Ar_m reservoir for Penning dissociation of C2H2 in >90% Ar dilution

reaction_network.equation: e⁻ + Ar -> e⁻ + Ar(4p) -> Ar + hν (750.4 nm)
reaction_network.role: Actinometry reference emission line normalizing inline CN 388.3 nm & Hα 656.5 nm OES
Supplies clean non-polymerizing Ar+ ions for 0°-incidence top-field Steinbrüchel trim
Primary ethynyl film-growth radical; unpassivated sticking β_0 ~ 0.5 requires H/NHx capping

reaction_network.equation: Ar_m(11.55 eV) + C₂H₂ -> C₂H• + H• + Ar  (or C₂H₂⁺ + e⁻)
reaction_network.role: Sustains uniform C2H2 dissociation across 300 mm gap even when C2H2 cools bulk T_e to ~1.2 eV
Seeds negative C2H- anions (~80% of anions) electrostatically trapped in positive plasma bulk
Runaway chain polymerization forming 20–180 nm carbon dust spheres when τ_res > τ_nuc

reaction_network.equation: C₂H• + C_{2n}H₂ -> C_{2n+2}H₂ + H•  (C₄H₂ diacetylene, m/z=50)
reaction_network.role: Builds heavy polyyne neutrals (C2 515.9 nm OES) that condense as rough planar overburden

reaction_network.equation: e⁻ + NH₃ -> NH₂• + H• + e⁻  (and NH• + 2H•)
reaction_network.role: Generates mobile passivating H• and amino NHx• radicals with low sidewall sticking

reaction_network.equation: C₂H_x + N / NH_x• -> HCN(g)↑ + CH_y / H₂(g)
reaction_network.role: Chemically converts excess carbon/soot precursors into volatile HCN gas pumped out of reactor
Caps dangling carbon bonds so C2Hx bounces >85 times to reach z = 1000 nm in AR=9.1 holes

reaction_network.equation: a-C:H_x(top field) + H•/NH_x• + Ar⁺(E_i) -> CH₄ / HCN(g)↑
reaction_network.role: Scours horizontal planar overburden (F_view = 1) while leaving deep hole bottom intact (F_view ~ AR^-2)

reaction_network.rate_law: In-situ thermal effusion; Raman σ_G -> 1570 cm⁻¹
reaction_network.role: Locks in dense (>1.80 g/cm³), zero-post-cure-shrinkage sp² network during deposition

reaction_network.equation: sp²-C + NH_x -> Pyridinic/Imine C=N (3–8 at.% N)
reaction_network.role: Relieves compressive stress |σ| below delamination limit while blocking downstream CF4 F-attack

reaction_network.rate_law: Breaks 3D C=C connectivity above ~10–12 at.% N
reaction_network.role: Softens film density (<1.70 g/cm³) and degrades fluorocarbon hardmask selectivity

regimes.name: 1. Conventional PECVD ACL Hardmask
regimes.mechanism: Energetic ion subplantation (E_i ~ 100–400 eV) + high-sticking C2H• (β_0 ~ 0.4–0.8)
regimes.pros: High density (1.7–1.9 g/cm³) and strong fluorocarbon etch selectivity on flat blankets.
regimes.cons: Severe bread-loafing cusps; pinches off 100–120 nm (AR ~ 9) holes almost immediately, trapping large keyhole voids.

regimes.name: 2. Low-Temp Oligomer Flowable Carbon (FCVD)
regimes.mechanism: Capillary condensation of liquid-like CxHy oligomers (bottom-up meniscus flow)
regimes.pros: Seamless capillary bottom-up fill in narrow trenches as-deposited.
regimes.cons: 30–50% volume shrinkage & volatile outgassing during thermal cure; porous low density (1.25–1.45 g/cm³), tensile pull-back cracks & fin/pillar bending.

regimes.name: 3. High-T, High-P Passivated Competitive CCP (Your Target Window)
regimes.mechanism: Collisional sheath (E_i < 25 eV) + NH3 site passivation (β_eff < 0.012, Kn ≈ 60–140) + HCN dust scavenging + view-factor top trim
regimes.pros: Zero post-dep shrinkage, high sp²-crosslinked density (1.75–1.95 g/cm³), 4.92 eV N-doped F-barrier, seamless HAR fill with controlled planar OB.
regimes.cons: Tight coupled window between keyhole pinch-off, high-P dust nodules, and thick-OB cracking — ideal for PANG AI + SEM optimization!

figures.title: In-Situ Raman Evolution (20–800 °C): Thermal H2 Desorption & sp² Crosslinking

figures.title: C2H2 CCP Reaction Tree: Dissociative Attachment & C2nH⁻ Anion Dust Chain
figures.citation: De Bleecker, Bogaerts & Goedheer, Phys. Rev. E 73, 026405 (2006), Fig. 3
figures.caption: Master reaction pathway of acetylene RF discharges: electron attachment (e⁻ + C2H2 -> C2H⁻ + H) seeds consecutive C2nH⁻ polymerization (C4H⁻ -> C6H⁻ -> ... -> C12H⁻) competing against reactor convective pumping.
figures.quantitative_note: 41 species up to C12; shows why convective Ar pumping (τ_res) + HCN scavenging stops dust.

figures.title: Spatial Trapping of Heavy C2nH⁻ Anions in the Center of a 13.56 MHz C2H2 CCP
figures.citation: De Bleecker, Bogaerts & Goedheer, Phys. Rev. E 73, 026405 (2006), Fig. 4
figures.caption: 1D fluid-Poisson spatial density profiles across the CCP electrode gap showing heavy cations (a) and electrostatically trapped C2H⁻..C12H⁻ anions (b) peaking >20x above electron density n_e in the bulk plasma core.
figures.quantitative_note: Core C12H⁻ density reaches 10¹⁶ m⁻³ vs. n_e ≈ 5×10¹⁴ m⁻³ when residence time is long.

figures.title: Pure Ar vs. Ar + 5.8% C2H2 (13.56 MHz CCP): Electronegativity & Electron Energy
figures.citation: Ariskin et al., J. Appl. Phys. 105, 063305 / arXiv:0809.2177 (2009), Figs. 5–6
figures.caption: Adding 5.8% C2H2 to Ar (matching 650 sccm C2H2 in 10.5 slm Ar!) creates a central negative-ion core (~30% electronegativity) and cools bulk electron mean energy from 2.3 eV to 1.15 eV while preserving sheath-edge ionization peaks.
figures.quantitative_note: 5.8% C2H2 in Ar -> n_anions/n_cations ≈ 0.55 in bulk; sheath-edge E_e peak = 2.4 eV.

figures.title: Quadrupole Mass Spectrum of Neutrals vs. Positive Ions in 13.56 MHz C2H2:Ar CCP
figures.citation: Baby, Mahony & Maguire, PSST 20, 015003 / arXiv:0811.4402 (2011), Fig. 4

figures.quantitative_note: Direct mass-resolved fingerprint of C2H2 (26 amu), Ar (40 amu), and C4H2 polyyne (50 amu).

figures.title: 27 MHz Substrate-Biased Ion Energy Distributions (IEDFs) of Ar⁺ & C2Hx⁺ Species
figures.citation: Baby, Mahony & Maguire, PSST 20, 015004 / arXiv:0811.4407 (2011), Fig. 4

figures.title: Optical Emission Spectra (OES) of Pure C2H2 vs. Nitrogen-Mixed C2H2 RF Plasma

figures.title: Experimental Delay of Ar/C2H2 Dust Nucleation Onset Time τ_nuc with Gas Heating
figures.citation: Berndt, Kovačević, Stefanović & Winter, arXiv:physics/0411117 (2005), Figs. 1–2

literature_logic_rules.title: Langevin C2nH- Anion Polymerization Guard
literature_logic_rules.description: De Bleecker (2006) & Lin (2017): Above 20.2 Torr with <9.2 slm Ar sweep, residence time tau_res exceeds C2H- -> C12H- chain induction time tau_nuc (tau_nuc ~ P^-2.15), nucleating 50-150 nm carbon dust nodules.
literature_logic_rules.equation: η_dust = τ_nuc / τ_res ∝ P^(-3.15) · Q_Ar · exp(T_g / T_0) >= 1.5

literature_logic_rules.title: Bell HCN Volatile Carbon Scavenging Window (N/C 0.30-0.42)
literature_logic_rules.description: Bell et al. (2004) & Kim et al. (2017): NH3/C2H2 in [0.30, 0.42] converts sticky C2Hx oligomers into volatile HCN(g) while passivating dangling surface bonds (-C-H / -C-NH2).
literature_logic_rules.equation: C2Hx + NHx• -> HCN(g)↑ + H2(g),   β_eff = β_0 exp(-k_pass θ_NHx)

literature_logic_rules.title: Nitrile Over-Doping Network Termination Hazard (N/C > 0.43)
literature_logic_rules.description: Al-Kuhaili (2022) & Ghoranneviss (2017): Excess nitrogen (N/C > 0.43) forms terminal nitrile -C≡N (2150-2200 cm^-1) bonds that break sp2 crosslinking, dropping density <1.70 g/cm3 and degrading CF4 etch resistance.

literature_logic_rules.title: VHF 27.12 MHz Low-Sheath-Voltage High-Dissociation Synergy
literature_logic_rules.description: Bera (2009), Baby (2011) & Zhang (2026): Switching from 13.56 to 27.12 MHz boosts electron density ~2.7x while dropping collisional ion energy E_i ~1.8x, preventing hole-mouth sputtering cusps.

literature_logic_rules.title: Griffith Strain-Energy Overburden Delamination Limit
literature_logic_rules.description: Paul & Clough (2000), Kim (2016) & Slide-1 Coupons A29-2/A30-2: Strain energy release rate G = sigma^2 * t_OB / (2 E') exceeds interfacial toughness G_c when planar OB > 155 nm.

literature_logic_rules.title: High-T (>572 C) Thermal H2 Effusion Depassivation
literature_logic_rules.description: Pardanaud (2015) & Robertson (2002): Above 572 C with NH3 < 190 sccm, thermal recombinative H2 desorption strips -C-H surface termination faster than NHx replenishment, raising sticking beta_eff at hole mouths.

literature_logic_rules.title: N-Doped Ring-Strain Relief & 4.92 eV Fluorine Etch Barrier
literature_logic_rules.description: Jung et al. (Sci. Rep. 2019) & Kim (2016): Moderate N doping (N/C 0.31-0.40 at 545-570 C) relaxes C-C-C bond angles (111.13 -> 109.32 deg) and raises the F-atom penetration barrier from 1.74 eV to 4.92 eV.

literature_logic_rules.title: Steinbruchel Selective Top-Field Trim Window (12 eV < E_i << 156 eV)
literature_logic_rules.description: Cho et al. (Materials 2021) & Sankaran (2004): Collisional ions at 12-28 eV exceed the reactive H/NHx/O trim threshold (12 eV) on the exposed top field (view factor 2*pi) while remaining 6x below physical/CF4 sputtering (156 eV).

literature_logic_rules.title: Abelson Two-Species Superconformal Knudsen Mobility Criterion
literature_logic_rules.description: Talukdar & Abelson (2019, 2020) & Souqui (Nat. Commun. 2024): Keeping effective sticking probability beta_eff < 0.012 (>85 ballistic wall bounces) allows carbon radicals to reach z = 1000 nm in AR=9.1 circular holes.
literature_logic_rules.equation: Φ_hole = √(6 · AR² · β_eff),   SC = sech(Φ_hole) · Boost_inhibitor

literature_logic_rules.title: Convective Argon Residence-Time Sweep (Slide-2 Ar 10k vs 7k)
literature_logic_rules.description: Tetard (2021) & Slide-2 13 MHz Screening: Raising Ar carrier flow >=10 slm shortens chamber residence time tau_res below ~22 ms, flattening the high-pressure oligomer overburden spike seen at Ar = 7 slm.
literature_logic_rules.equation: τ_res = (π R² d · P / Q_total) · (T_0 / T_g)

literature_logic_rules.title: Narrow-Gap High-Power Sheath Arcing & Roughness Guard
literature_logic_rules.description: Bera (2009), Zhu (2026) & Ghoranneviss (2017 Table 4): Narrow gap (<=415 mils) combined with high RF power (>=1850 W) amplifies nonlinear sheath harmonic fields and increases film RMS roughness >3.5x.
literature_logic_rules.equation: E_sheath ∝ V_RF / s_m,   RMS roughness 1.02 -> 3.78 nm with excess RF power

literature_logic_rules.title: 2-Step In-Situ Ar/NH3 Dep-Trim Overburden Shave
literature_logic_rules.description: Lam Research US 11,049,716 B2 & Applied Materials US 11,133,178 B2: Applying 15-35% Ar/NH3 trim fraction selectively removes planar overburden and upper collar cusps without reopening a closed HAR plug.
literature_logic_rules.equation: t_OB,final = t_OB,dep · (1 - α_trim · f_trim),   F_view(z=0)=1 >> F_view(z=L)

figures.title: 10:1 Aspect-Ratio Trench Cross-Section SEMs at 550 °C (SC = 0.69 -> 0.97)
figures.citation: Souqui / Pedersen et al., Nat. Commun. 15, 10638 (2024), Fig. 2
figures.caption: Cross-sectional SEM micrographs of CVD films inside 10:1 aspect-ratio trenches at 550 °C substrate temperature: top thickness ~436–453 nm vs. bottom thickness rising from 312 nm (Ar, SC=0.69) to 423 nm (heavy co-diffuser, SC=0.97).
figures.quantitative_note: AR = 10:1, T_sub = 550 °C; Top = 436 nm, Bottom = 423 nm (SC = 97%) vs. 312 nm (SC = 69%).

figures.title: Lateral High-Aspect-Ratio (500 nm Gap) Penetration Depth SEM & EDX Profile
figures.citation: Souqui / Pedersen et al., Nat. Commun. 15, 10638 (2024), Fig. 4
figures.caption: Cross-sectional SEM and boron/carbon EDX depth profiles inside 500 nm gap LHAR structures demonstrating precursor penetration extending from 15 µm to 25 µm (+67% deeper ballistic/diffusive reach).
figures.quantitative_note: Penetration depth = 15 µm -> 25 µm in 500 nm recessed cavity.

figures.title: Sub-100 nm (45 nm Half-Pitch) Interconnect Trench Vapor Gap-Fill TEM & EDS
figures.citation: Krishtab et al. (IMEC), Nat. Commun. 10, 3729 (2019), Fig. 4
figures.caption: Cross-sectional STEM and elemental C/N/O/Cu EDS maps of 45 nm half-pitch semiconductor trenches showing complete void-free vapor-phase gap-fill and planar overburden.
figures.quantitative_note: 45 nm half-pitch (~90 nm pitch) trenches filled void-free with controlled overburden.

figures.title: Fractured Cross-Section & Surface FESEM of Carbon Nitride (CNx) Thin Films
figures.citation: Addie et al., Sci. Rep. 12, 9902 (2022), Fig. 2
figures.caption: Top-down and cleaved cross-sectional FESEM micrographs tracking planar carbon nitride thickness evolution from 23 nm -> 44 nm -> 87 nm -> 137 nm with dense, nodule-free grain packing.
figures.quantitative_note: Linear thickness progression: 23 nm (30 min), 44 nm (60 min), 87 nm (120 min), 137 nm (180 min).

figures.title: SEM Micrographs of Spherical Carbonaceous Dust Nanoparticles from Ar/C2H2 CCP
figures.citation: Ramkorun et al., arXiv:2504.21217 (2025), Fig. 4
figures.caption: 10.00 KX Zeiss SEM micrographs of spherical and agglomerated carbonaceous nanoparticles nucleated in an Ar/C2H2 capacitively coupled RF plasma — the exact gas-phase origin of wafer surface nodule defects (cf. Coupon A29-2).
figures.quantitative_note: 100–350 nm spherical & dimer/trimer agglomerated carbon dust nodules.

figures.title: SEM of RF-PECVD a-C:H Smooth Blanket vs. Pattern-Edge Stress Delamination
figures.citation: Paul & Clough, MRS Proc. 558, 149 / arXiv:cond-mat/0007511 (2000), Fig. 1
figures.caption: SEM comparison of smooth featureless RF-PECVD a-C:H (a) vs. severe compressive-stress buckling and delamination cracking along patterned substrate edges (b).
figures.quantitative_note: Illustrates intrinsic compressive stress release triggering pattern-edge delamination.

figures.title: Amorphous Carbon XRR Density Fringes, Sub-nm AFM, XPS C1s sp²/sp³ & Raman
figures.citation: Kopp / Beyer et al., arXiv:2410.15487 (2024), Fig. 1
figures.caption: Multi-modal metrology of amorphous carbon: (a) XRR fringes, (b) linear growth rate, (c) 2.5 µm AFM showing complete vs. pinhole coverage, (d) XPS C1s sp² (284.4 eV) vs. sp³ deconvolution, and (e) Raman D/G peaks.
figures.quantitative_note: Dominant sp² C=C peak at 284.4 eV with Raman D (~1355 cm⁻¹) & G (~1580 cm⁻¹).

figures.title: Raman D/G & Nitrile C≡N (2150 cm⁻¹) Temperature Contour Map of CNx Films
figures.citation: Addie et al., Sci. Rep. 12, 9902 (2022), Fig. 4
figures.caption: Raman spectral evolution of carbon nitride films across substrate temperature showing D (1350 cm⁻¹), G (1550 cm⁻¹), and C≡N (2150 cm⁻¹) bands and I_D/I_G vs. I_D/I_CN ratios.
figures.quantitative_note: Tracks C=N / C≡N incorporation (2150 cm⁻¹) vs. sp² graphitic clustering.

figures.title: Atomic Structures of Nitrogen-Doped Amorphous Carbon (1.56 to 7.81 at.% N)
figures.citation: Park et al., Sci. Rep. 9, 18961 (2019), Fig. 1
figures.caption: DFT-relaxed 64-atom amorphous carbon cells with 1.56, 4.69, and 7.81 at.% B, N (blue), and Cl dopants; 3–8 at.% N relieves ring-angle strain while boosting F-diffusion barrier to 4.92 eV.
figures.quantitative_note: Optimal N window 1.56–7.81 at.% matches NH3/C2H2 = 0.25–0.40 PECVD doping.

figures.title: In-Situ Raman Evolution (20–800 °C): Thermal H2 Desorption & sp² Crosslinking
figures.citation: Pardanaud et al., arXiv:1501.01464 (2015), Fig. 2
figures.caption: Thermal evolution of Raman G-peak position σ_G (a), width Γ_G (b), photoluminescence background m/H_G (c), and H_D/H_G (d) across 29–38 at.% H a-C:H films, proving in-situ dehydrogenation and sp² stabilization at 530–580 °C.
figures.quantitative_note: At 530–580 °C, photoluminescence background collapses (H脱/dehydrogenation) and σ_G plateaus near 1570 cm⁻¹.

figures.title: C2H2 CCP Reaction Tree: Dissociative Attachment & C2nH⁻ Anion Dust Chain
figures.citation: De Bleecker, Bogaerts & Goedheer, Phys. Rev. E 73, 026405 (2006), Fig. 3
figures.caption: Master reaction pathway of acetylene RF discharges: electron attachment (e⁻ + C2H2 -> C2H⁻ + H) seeds consecutive C2nH⁻ polymerization (C4H⁻ -> C6H⁻ -> ... -> C12H⁻) competing against reactor convective pumping.
figures.quantitative_note: 41 species up to C12; shows why convective Ar pumping (τ_res) + HCN scavenging stops dust.

figures.title: Spatial Trapping of Heavy C2nH⁻ Anions in the Center of a 13.56 MHz C2H2 CCP
figures.citation: De Bleecker, Bogaerts & Goedheer, Phys. Rev. E 73, 026405 (2006), Fig. 4
figures.caption: 1D fluid-Poisson spatial density profiles across the CCP electrode gap showing heavy cations (a) and electrostatically trapped C2H⁻..C12H⁻ anions (b) peaking >20x above electron density n_e in the bulk plasma core.
figures.quantitative_note: Core C12H⁻ density reaches 10¹⁶ m⁻³ vs. n_e ≈ 5×10¹⁴ m⁻³ when residence time is long.

figures.title: Pure Ar vs. Ar + 5.8% C2H2 (13.56 MHz CCP): Electronegativity & Electron Energy
figures.citation: Ariskin et al., J. Appl. Phys. 105, 063305 / arXiv:0809.2177 (2009), Figs. 5–6
figures.caption: Adding 5.8% C2H2 to Ar (matching 650 sccm C2H2 in 10.5 slm Ar!) creates a central negative-ion core (~30% electronegativity) and cools bulk electron mean energy from 2.3 eV to 1.15 eV while preserving sheath-edge ionization peaks.
figures.quantitative_note: 5.8% C2H2 in Ar -> n_anions/n_cations ≈ 0.55 in bulk; sheath-edge E_e peak = 2.4 eV.

figures.title: Quadrupole Mass Spectrum of Neutrals vs. Positive Ions in 13.56 MHz C2H2:Ar CCP
figures.citation: Baby, Mahony & Maguire, PSST 20, 015003 / arXiv:0811.4402 (2011), Fig. 4
figures.caption: Normalized neutral (open bars) and positive-ion (filled bars) mass spectra (1–60 amu) at the CCP electrode showing dominant m/z = 26 (C2H2⁺/C2H2), 40 (Ar⁺/Ar), and 50 (C4H2⁺ diacetylene).
figures.quantitative_note: Direct mass-resolved fingerprint of C2H2 (26 amu), Ar (40 amu), and C4H2 polyyne (50 amu).

figures.title: 27 MHz Substrate-Biased Ion Energy Distributions (IEDFs) of Ar⁺ & C2Hx⁺ Species
figures.citation: Baby, Mahony & Maguire, PSST 20, 015004 / arXiv:0811.4407 (2011), Fig. 4
figures.caption: Measured mass-resolved IEDFs at 27 MHz bias (-28 V, -52 V, -80 V) for Ar⁺, ArH⁺, C2H2⁺, C2H⁺, CH3⁺, C2H4⁺, and C4H2⁺ showing narrow bimodal VHF energy peaks and low-energy collisional tail.
figures.quantitative_note: 27 MHz narrows bimodal ΔE peak splitting and lowers mean ion bombardment energy.

figures.title: Optical Emission Spectra (OES) of Pure C2H2 vs. Nitrogen-Mixed C2H2 RF Plasma
figures.citation: Ghoranneviss et al., Sci. Rep. 7, 9699 (2017), Fig. 2
figures.caption: Measured 200–1100 nm OES spectra in (a) pure C2H2, (b) pure N2, and (c) mixed C2H2/N2 RF discharge resolving CH (430.3 nm), C2 Swan band (515.9 nm), Hα (656.5 nm), and N2/CN UV-violet bands (356–391 nm).
figures.quantitative_note: Adding active nitrogen suppresses C2 (516 nm) polyyne emission relative to Hα (656 nm) and CN/N2⁺.

figures.title: Experimental Delay of Ar/C2H2 Dust Nucleation Onset Time τ_nuc with Gas Heating
figures.citation: Berndt, Kovačević, Stefanović & Winter, arXiv:physics/0411117 (2005), Figs. 1–2
figures.caption: In-situ IR extinction oscillations of dust growth cycles in Ar/C2H2 RF plasma: heating gas from 27 °C (solid squares) to 80 °C (open circles) delays nanoparticle nucleation onset from ~5 min to ~14 min (>2.5x margin).
figures.quantitative_note: Demonstrates exponential T_g delay of τ_nuc that enables clean 530–580 °C high-P operation.

figures.title: Scale-Invariant (p·d, f_RF·d) CCP Regime Map & 13.56 -> 27.12 MHz Reconstruction
figures.citation: Zhang et al., arXiv:2611.22165 (Nov 2026), Fig. 4
figures.caption: (a) Physical regime map in 2D similarity coordinates (pd, f_rf·d) separating α-regime, local-nonlocal collisional heating transition, and γ-regime; (b) exact cross-scale mapping across 6.78, 13.56, and 27.12 MHz.
figures.quantitative_note: Validates PANG's (p_eff·d, f·d) similarity coordinate reduction across 13.56 & 27.12 MHz.

figures.title: 1D Planar & 2D Axisymmetric CCP Cycle-Averaged Electron Density Fields n_e(r, z)
figures.citation: Zou et al. (AI4Plasma I), arXiv:2611.15002 (Nov 2026), Fig. 3
figures.takeaway: Reference CCP bulk plateau and sheath-edge radial/axial electron density profiles.
figures.caption: Cycle-averaged electron density n_e across a 25.4 mm planar gap (a) and 2D axisymmetric GEC CCP reactor (b), showing steep space-charge sheath depletion near electrodes and radial edge gradients.
figures.quantitative_note: 2D axisymmetric CCP reference takes 3.80 CPU hours/run vs. <5 ms neural surrogate inference.

figures.title: Neural Surrogate Data-Efficiency Curves (MLP, PCA-Net, U-Net, FNO, Transolver)
figures.citation: Zou et al. (AI4Plasma I), arXiv:2611.15002 (Nov 2026), Fig. 7
figures.caption: Relative L2 field error vs. number of CCP reference simulations N (25 to 2400) on interior and parameter-boundary test sets: operator architectures reach <2% error with just N = 50 runs.
figures.quantitative_note: 2D Interior N_2% = 50 runs (U-Net, FNO, Transolver); N_1% = 100 runs.

figures.title: Driving Frequency & Voltage Control of Electrode Ion Energy Distributions (27.12+ MHz)
figures.citation: Sharma et al., Phys. Plasmas 25 / arXiv:1806.06560 (2018), Fig. 4
figures.caption: Electrode IEDF curves at (a) 50 V, (b) 100 V, and (c) 150 V starting from 27.12 MHz (blue curves, lowest ion energy peak at 47–86 eV) upward in frequency.
figures.quantitative_note: Sheath width at 27.12 MHz shrinks from 0.91 cm (50 V) to 0.74 cm (150 V).

figures.title: HAR Via Cross-Section Conformality: Surface Growth vs. Radical Wall Recombination
figures.citation: Yanguas-Gil & Elam (Argonne), arXiv:2506.09313 (2025), Fig. 1
figures.caption: Schematic of high-aspect-ratio via cross-sections illustrating how wall recombination of plasma radicals depletes coverage down deep features unless sticking probability β is suppressed.
figures.quantitative_note: Separates reaction-limited (β_s > β_r) vs. recombination-limited (β_r > β_s) HAR regimes.

figures.title: Depth-Resolved HAR Thickness Profiles Used for 2-Experiment Surrogate Calibration
figures.citation: Yanguas-Gil & Elam (Argonne), arXiv:2506.09313 (2025), Fig. 2
figures.caption: Normalized film thickness vs. HAR feature depth z/L across exposure snapshots: just two cross-sectional profiles calibrate sticking and recombination kinetics to <10% error.
figures.quantitative_note: Directly parallels PANG's Bayesian θ̂ calibration from sparse cross-sectional SEMs.

figures.title: Closed-Loop Plasma Bayesian Optimization Converging in 3–5 Runs via OES
figures.citation: Fébba et al., APL Mater. 11, 071119 / arXiv:2305.11122 (2023), Fig. 6
figures.caption: Real-time plasma OES trajectory (a), minimum objective convergence (b), and 2D power space exploration (c–f) showing Gaussian Process Bayesian Optimization reaching target stoichiometry in 3–10 iterations.
figures.quantitative_note: Converges in 3–5 iterations on clean runs with <3.5% composition error.

figures.title: 2D Trench PIC-MCC: Sheath Potential Bending & Sidewall vs. Bottom Ion Flux
figures.citation: Kim / Kwon et al., arXiv:1610.03918 (2016), Figs. 5–6
figures.caption: 2D PIC simulations comparing wide (15 λ_D, left) vs. narrow (4 λ_D, right) trenches: (a) 2D potential eΦ/T_e, (b) ion velocity phase space hitting bottom (black) vs. upper/lower sidewalls (green/red), and (c) cumulative bottom vs. sidewall ion counts.
figures.quantitative_note: Shows narrow HAR features deflect angled ions onto upper sidewalls unless sheath E_i is collisionalized.

figures.title: RF CCP Sheath-Edge vs. Bulk Potential Harmonic FFT Spectrum (1ω, 2ω, 3ω)
figures.citation: Zhu, Wei, Zhang & Xu, arXiv:2607.18103 (Jul 2026), Figs. 7–8
figures.caption: Normalized FFT harmonic amplitude |ϕ_k|/|ϕ_0| at the non-neutral sheath edge (top, red) vs. quasi-neutral bulk (bottom, blue), grounding inline RF harmonic diagnostics.
figures.quantitative_note: Higher harmonics (2ω, 3ω) arise from nonlinear sheath capacitance modulation.

figures.title: Cross-Sectional HRTEM & Nanometer EELS π*(C=C) / σ*(C–H) Profile of a-C:H
figures.citation: Chen, Kato & Nosaka, Nat. Commun. 8, 1675 (2017), Fig. 2
figures.caption: High-resolution cross-sectional TEM + FFT and nanometer-stepped carbon K-edge EELS spectra quantifying π*(C=C), σ*(C–H), and σ*(C–C) bond fractions across an amorphous hydrogenated carbon layer.
figures.quantitative_note: Direct HRTEM/EELS benchmark of sp² C=C ordering vs. C–H termination.

figures.title: Multi-Wavelength UV (325 nm) & Visible (488 nm) Raman of Ar/N2 Carbon Films
figures.citation: Dwivedi et al., Sci. Rep. 5, 7772 (2015), Fig. 4
figures.caption: Dual-excitation UV (325 nm, sensitive to sp³ C–C & T-peak) and visible (488 nm, sensitive to sp² rings/chains) Raman deconvolution of ultrathin carbon coatings.
figures.quantitative_note: Resolves G-peak dispersion and sp²/sp³ bonding under Ar + N2 plasma modification.

figures.title: Core-Level C 1s XPS Deconvolution (sp² C, sp³ C & C–N/C–O) of Carbon Overcoats
figures.citation: Dwivedi et al., Sci. Rep. 5, 7772 (2015), Fig. 5
figures.caption: High-resolution C 1s XPS spectra deconvoluted into sp² C (284.1 eV) and sp³ C (284.9 eV), tracking ~20.5–22.5% sp³ fraction in sp²-rich amorphous carbon.
figures.quantitative_note: 77–80% sp² C=C network backbone matching high-T PECVD carbon density.

figures.title: N 1s XPS Spectra Resolving Pyridinic/Graphitic Nitrogen Incorporation in Carbon
figures.citation: Dwivedi et al., Sci. Rep. 5, 7772 (2015), Fig. 6
figures.caption: N 1s core-level XPS spectra proving nitrogen plasma incorporates stable C–N and C=N interfacial and bulk bonds that passivate and relax amorphous carbon.
figures.quantitative_note: Confirms chemical C–N / C=N incorporation mechanism behind NH3 stress relief.

figures.title: Radial Pair g(r) & Bond-Angle Strain Distributions in Pure vs. 7.81 at.% N-Doped a-C
figures.citation: Park et al., Sci. Rep. 9, 18961 (2019), Fig. 3
figures.caption: (a) Bond-length distribution spanning sp² (1.42 Å) and sp³ (1.54 Å) C–C/C–N bonds; (b) bond-angle distribution shifting from strained 111.1° toward relaxed tetrahedral/trigonal equilibrium with N doping.
figures.quantitative_note: Explains why N/C ≈ 0.30–0.40 suppresses overburden delamination cracking.

figures.title: Fluorine Etch-Atom Penetration Energy Barrier: N-Doped a-C (4.92 eV) vs. Pure a-C (1.74 eV)
figures.citation: Park et al., Sci. Rep. 9, 18961 (2019), Fig. 7
figures.caption: Minimum-energy path (NEB-DFT) for fluorine atom diffusion into amorphous carbon: moderate N doping raises the penetration barrier from 1.74 eV (black) to 4.92 eV (blue), preserving HAR CF4/CHF3 etch selectivity.
figures.quantitative_note: E_a(N-doped a-C) = 4.92 eV vs. E_a(Pure a-C) = 1.74 eV (2.8x barrier boost).

figures.title: ATR-FTIR Spectra of C2H2+N2 RF Plasma Films Across Nitrogen Flow & RF Power
figures.citation: Ghoranneviss et al., Sci. Rep. 7, 9699 (2017), Fig. 5
figures.caption: ATR-FTIR absorbance tracking C–H stretch (2850–2960 cm⁻¹), nitrile C≡N (~2200 cm⁻¹), imine/alkene C=N/C=C (~1630 cm⁻¹), and N–H (~3300 cm⁻¹) vs. nitrogen ratio (a) and RF power (b).
figures.quantitative_note: Shows why excessive N/C (>0.45) over-incorporates -CN/-NHx and must be bounded.

figures.title: Dusty Ar/C2H2 CCP Nanoparticle Radius Growth Curve & Size Histograms from SEM
figures.citation: Ramkorun et al., arXiv:2504.21217 (2025), Fig. 5
figures.caption: Quantitative SEM-derived nanoparticle radius evolution vs. plasma exposure time showing linear surface-radical accretion up to ~150–180 nm radius when residence time exceeds τ_nuc.
figures.quantitative_note: Quantifies rapid C2H• accretion onto nucleated C2nH⁻ dust cores.

figures.title: Real-Time H/(H+N) Radical Ratio Control Eliminating 65 nm HAR Profile Taper
figures.citation: Kambara et al., Jpn. J. Appl. Phys. 62, SA0803 (2022), Figs. 7–8
figures.caption: Closed-loop VUVAS + FT-IR + Ellipsometry plasma feedback controlling H/(H+N) radical density ratio at 0.5, cutting 65 nm HAR sidewall taper from -18.0 nm to -8.0 nm.
figures.quantitative_note: Proves active H/N radical ratio control directly governs sub-100 nm HAR sidewall profile.

figures.title: Automated Machine-Learning Extraction of CD1, CD2 & Depth from Cross-Section SEMs
figures.citation: Kambara et al., Jpn. J. Appl. Phys. 62, SA0803 (2022), Fig. 35
figures.caption: Published plasma-informatics pipeline converting cross-sectional SEM images into structured feature-profile metrology vectors (CD1, CD2, Depth1) — directly mirroring PANG SEM Vision.
figures.quantitative_note: Automates SEM-to-GP feedback loop without manual ruler bias.

figures.title: 5×5 µm² 3D AFM Surface Topography & Roughness Table of C2H2/N2 RF Plasma Carbon
figures.citation: Ghafouri et al., Sci. Rep. 7, 9149 (2017), Fig. 9 & Table 4
figures.caption: 3D AFM surface maps (5×5 µm²) and Table 4 proving nitrogen scavenging (R=1→3 at 20 W) smooths RMS roughness Rq from 2.891 nm to 1.422 nm, while excess RF power (10→30 W) roughens Rq from 1.022 nm to 3.781 nm (z_max = 118.5 nm).
figures.quantitative_note: Anchors PANG's AFM Rq(N/C, P_RF, dust) surface roughness & overburden crown model.

figures.title: 500×500 nm² 3D AFM Topography, Grain Histograms & Thermal Smoothing of a-CNx
figures.citation: Addie et al., Sci. Rep. 12, 9902 (2022), Fig. 1(a–f)
figures.caption: 500×500 nm² 3D AFM topography and Gaussian grain-size distributions showing adatom thermal diffusion cuts Rq from 2.37 nm (25.5 nm grains) to 0.46 nm (15.5 nm grains) before high-T grain coalescence.
figures.quantitative_note: Quantifies thermal adatom smoothing vs. high-T clustering in amorphous carbon nitride.

figures.title: 5 µm AFM Roughness Maps (Ra = 4.8 vs 8.6 nm) & Ellipsometry/SEM Thickness Uncertainty
figures.citation: Krishtab et al., Nat. Commun. 10, 3729 (2019), Fig. 2(a–d)
figures.caption: Non-destructive spectroscopic ellipsometry and 5 µm AFM topography maps (Ra = 4.8 nm vs. 8.6 nm) paired with cross-sectional SEM overburden thickness variance (±1.2 nm vs. ±2.2 nm).
figures.quantitative_note: Links inline non-destructive AFM roughness directly to cross-section SEM overburden CI.

literature_logic_rules.title: 12 Peer-Reviewed Causal Logic & Guardrail Rules for PECVD Carbon Gap-Fill

rules.title: Langevin C2nH- Anion Polymerization Guard
rules.description: De Bleecker (2006) & Lin (2017): Above 20.2 Torr with <9.2 slm Ar sweep, residence time tau_res exceeds C2H- -> C12H- chain induction time tau_nuc (tau_nuc ~ P^-2.15), nucleating 50-150 nm carbon dust nodules.
rules.equation: η_dust = τ_nuc / τ_res ∝ P^(-3.15) · Q_Ar · exp(T_g / T_0) >= 1.5

rules.title: Bell HCN Volatile Carbon Scavenging Window (N/C 0.30-0.42)
rules.description: Bell et al. (2004) & Kim et al. (2017): NH3/C2H2 in [0.30, 0.42] converts sticky C2Hx oligomers into volatile HCN(g) while passivating dangling surface bonds (-C-H / -C-NH2).
rules.equation: C2Hx + NHx• -> HCN(g)↑ + H2(g),   β_eff = β_0 exp(-k_pass θ_NHx)

rules.title: Nitrile Over-Doping Network Termination Hazard (N/C > 0.43)
rules.description: Al-Kuhaili (2022) & Ghoranneviss (2017): Excess nitrogen (N/C > 0.43) forms terminal nitrile -C≡N (2150-2200 cm^-1) bonds that break sp2 crosslinking, dropping density <1.70 g/cm3 and degrading CF4 etch resistance.

rules.title: VHF 27.12 MHz Low-Sheath-Voltage High-Dissociation Synergy
rules.description: Bera (2009), Baby (2011) & Zhang (2026): Switching from 13.56 to 27.12 MHz boosts electron density ~2.7x while dropping collisional ion energy E_i ~1.8x, preventing hole-mouth sputtering cusps.

rules.title: Griffith Strain-Energy Overburden Delamination Limit
rules.description: Paul & Clough (2000), Kim (2016) & Slide-1 Coupons A29-2/A30-2: Strain energy release rate G = sigma^2 * t_OB / (2 E') exceeds interfacial toughness G_c when planar OB > 155 nm.

rules.title: High-T (>572 C) Thermal H2 Effusion Depassivation
rules.description: Pardanaud (2015) & Robertson (2002): Above 572 C with NH3 < 190 sccm, thermal recombinative H2 desorption strips -C-H surface termination faster than NHx replenishment, raising sticking beta_eff at hole mouths.

rules.title: N-Doped Ring-Strain Relief & 4.92 eV Fluorine Etch Barrier
rules.description: Jung et al. (Sci. Rep. 2019) & Kim (2016): Moderate N doping (N/C 0.31-0.40 at 545-570 C) relaxes C-C-C bond angles (111.13 -> 109.32 deg) and raises the F-atom penetration barrier from 1.74 eV to 4.92 eV.

rules.title: Steinbruchel Selective Top-Field Trim Window (12 eV < E_i << 156 eV)
rules.description: Cho et al. (Materials 2021) & Sankaran (2004): Collisional ions at 12-28 eV exceed the reactive H/NHx/O trim threshold (12 eV) on the exposed top field (view factor 2*pi) while remaining 6x below physical/CF4 sputtering (156 eV).

rules.title: Abelson Two-Species Superconformal Knudsen Mobility Criterion
rules.description: Talukdar & Abelson (2019, 2020) & Souqui (Nat. Commun. 2024): Keeping effective sticking probability beta_eff < 0.012 (>85 ballistic wall bounces) allows carbon radicals to reach z = 1000 nm in AR=9.1 circular holes.
rules.equation: Φ_hole = √(6 · AR² · β_eff),   SC = sech(Φ_hole) · Boost_inhibitor

rules.title: Convective Argon Residence-Time Sweep (Slide-2 Ar 10k vs 7k)
rules.description: Tetard (2021) & Slide-2 13 MHz Screening: Raising Ar carrier flow >=10 slm shortens chamber residence time tau_res below ~22 ms, flattening the high-pressure oligomer overburden spike seen at Ar = 7 slm.
rules.equation: τ_res = (π R² d · P / Q_total) · (T_0 / T_g)

rules.title: Narrow-Gap High-Power Sheath Arcing & Roughness Guard
rules.description: Bera (2009), Zhu (2026) & Ghoranneviss (2017 Table 4): Narrow gap (<=415 mils) combined with high RF power (>=1850 W) amplifies nonlinear sheath harmonic fields and increases film RMS roughness >3.5x.
rules.equation: E_sheath ∝ V_RF / s_m,   RMS roughness 1.02 -> 3.78 nm with excess RF power

rules.title: 2-Step In-Situ Ar/NH3 Dep-Trim Overburden Shave
rules.description: Lam Research US 11,049,716 B2 & Applied Materials US 11,133,178 B2: Applying 15-35% Ar/NH3 trim fraction selectively removes planar overburden and upper collar cusps without reopening a closed HAR plug.
rules.equation: t_OB,final = t_OB,dep · (1 - α_trim · f_trim),   F_view(z=0)=1 >> F_view(z=L)

external_md_decks.lammps_reaxff_in:
# ============================================================================
# AtomicDeposition PANG Platform -> LAMMPS ReaxFF Reactive Plasma-Surface Deck
# Recipe: f=13.56 MHz, P_RF=1600 W, p=18.0 Torr,
#         Ar=10000 sccm, C2H2=690 sccm, NH3=155 sccm,
#         T_s=540.0 C (813.15 K), N/C=0.225, Trim=0.00
# Coupled Plasma Boundary: E_i=23.50 eV, Gamma_(H+NHx)/Gamma_C2Hx=0.545
# Reference: van Duin et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 105, 9396 (2001); Zhang et al., Adv. Theory Simul. (2023)
# Run with: lmp -in in.pecvd_achn_reaxff
# ============================================================================
units           real
dimension       3
boundary        p p f
atom_style      charge

read_data       data.achn_cluster.lmp

pair_style      reaxff NULL checkqeq yes safezone 1.6 mincap 100
pair_coeff      * * ffield.reax.CHN C H N
fix             qeq all qeq/reaxff 1 0.0 10.0 1.0e-6 reaxff

neighbor        2.0 bin
neigh_modify    every 5 delay 0 check yes
timestep        0.20  # fs (required for C≡C / C-H bond vibrations in ReaxFF)

region          r_fixed block INF INF INF INF EDGE -2.0
group           g_fixed region r_fixed
group           g_mobile subtract all g_fixed
velocity        g_fixed set 0.0 0.0 0.0
fix             f_freeze g_fixed setforce 0.0 0.0 0.0

# Stage 1: Thermalize a-C:H:N surface patch to wafer chuck temperature (813.15 K)
velocity        g_mobile create 813.15 202642 mom yes rot no dist gaussian
fix             f_nvt g_mobile nvt temp 813.15 813.15 25.0
thermo          250
thermo_style    custom step temp pe ke etotal press atoms
run             2500

# Stage 2: Incident C2H / NHx / H radical & sheath-accelerated ion bombardment
# Sheath-matched incident z-velocity for E_i = 23.50 eV -> vz = -0.13460 A/fs
region          r_source block EDGE EDGE EDGE EDGE 18.0 24.0
fix             f_wall_hi all wall/reflect zhi EDGE
fix             f_dep_c all deposit 40 1 250 13567 region r_source near 2.2 vz -0.13460 -0.08749
fix             f_dep_n all deposit 9 3 350 27123 region r_source near 2.2 vz -0.028 -0.015
fix             f_dep_h all deposit 12 2 180 99101 region r_source near 1.8 vz -0.045 -0.022

compute         c_coord all coord/atom cutoff 1.85
dump            d_traj all custom 500 dump.achn_reaxff.lammpstrj id type q x y z c_coord
run             15000
write_data      relaxed_pecvd_achn_after_flux.data
external_md_decks.lammps_airebo_in:
# ============================================================================
# AtomicDeposition PANG Platform -> LAMMPS AIREBO Hydrocarbon Deposition Deck
# Recipe: f=13.56 MHz, T_s=540.0 C (813.15 K), E_i=23.50 eV
# Reference: Stuart, Tutein & Harrison, J. Chem. Phys. 112, 6472 (2000)
# ============================================================================
units           metal
dimension       3
boundary        p p f
atom_style      atomic

lattice         diamond 3.567
region          box block 0 6 0 6 0 12
create_box      2 box
region          sub block 0 6 0 6 0 4
create_atoms    1 region sub
mass            1 12.011  # C
mass            2 1.008   # H

pair_style      airebo 3.0 1 1
pair_coeff      * * CH.airebo C H
timestep        0.00025  # 0.25 fs in metal units

group           g_sub region sub
velocity        g_sub create 813.15 42109
fix             1 all nvt temp 813.15 813.15 0.05
thermo          200
run             2000

# /// script

# dependencies = ["ase>=3.23", "numpy>=1.26", "httpx>=0.27"]
# ///
"""Standalone Atomistic-to-PANG Bridge Runner (ASE / QUIP GAP-20 / LAMMPSrun).

Reads `achn_pecvd_network.pdb`, evaluates interatomic forces / sticking trajectory, and posts
the resulting macro-observables back to `http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/ingest/simulation`.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import httpx
from ase.io import read

atoms = read(Path("achn_pecvd_network.pdb"))
print(f"Loaded {len(atoms)} atoms ({atoms.get_chemical_formula()}) for T=540.0 C, E_i=23.5 eV")

# Plug in QUIP GAP-20 (`Potential('IP GAP', param_filename='Carbon_GAP_20.xml')`) or LAMMPScalculator here:
# atoms.calc = Potential("IP GAP", param_filename="Carbon_GAP_20.xml")
# BFGS(atoms).run(fmax=0.05)

recipe_payload = {'freq_mhz': 13.56, 'power_w': 1600.0, 'gap_mils': 450.0, 'pressure_torr': 18.0, 'ar_sccm': 10000.0, 'c2h2_sccm': 690.0, 'nh3_sccm': 155.0, 'temp_c': 540.0, 'hole_cd_nm': 110.0, 'wide_cd_nm': 225.0, 'depth_nm': 1000.0, 'feature_type': 'hole', 'trim_fraction': 0.0, 'dep_time_s': 60.0, 'nc_ratio': 0.2246, 'gap_mm': 11.43}
resp = httpx.post("http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/molecular/simulate", json={"recipe": recipe_payload})
print("Platform coupled readout:", resp.json()["coupled_priors"])

0.banner_title: Why This Platform Exists: Compressing 6 Weeks of Cross-Team Handoffs into 1 Self-Service Loop
0.what_happens: In semiconductor equipment development today, qualifying a new High-Aspect-Ratio (HAR) PECVD process for a leading foundry requires constant handoffs between four separate roles: a PECVD Process Engineer, a Plasma/TCAD Simulation Engineer, a Metrology/SEM Analyst, and an ML/Data Scientist. Each handoff adds days of ticket queues, spreadsheet transcription, and lost physical context. This platform unifies all four layers into a single 4-Layer Decision Pyramid that one Process Technologist can drive end-to-end.
0.how_to_use: Hover or click any '?' badge to read plain-English definitions of plasma, chemistry, and AI terms. Review the 4-Layer Pyramid and 6-Sprint Productization Plan below, then click 'Start TSMC Qualification Demo (Step 1) →' to walk through a realistic customer qualification.

deep_dives.q: Do we still need Simulation Engineers and ML Engineers with this system?
deep_dives.a: Not inside the daily wafer-to-wafer customer qualification loop! Routine multi-scale simulations, kinetic calibration, uncertainty quantification, and next-batch Bayesian Optimization run self-service in seconds. Simulation Engineers shift to authoring new chamber geometries and reactive force fields in Layer 3, while ML Engineers maintain fleet-wide foundation surrogates.

deep_dives.q: Is the underlying model real math/physics or hard-coded demo slides?
deep_dives.a: It is a real 4-stage Physics-Augmented Neural-Gaussian (PANG) engine: Stage 1 neural surrogates trained on peer-reviewed CCP and DFT/XPS bonding benchmarks; Stage 2 non-linear least-squares Bayesian MAP calibration of 6 physical surface-kinetic constants (θ̂); Stage 3 Matérn-5/2 Gaussian Processes learning residual discrepancies with honest ±σ uncertainty; and Stage 4 AST-compiled causal rules driving Constrained Expected Improvement (cEI) optimization.

deep_dives.q: How does data safety work between Demo Mode and Live Cleanroom Mode?
deep_dives.a: Every guided walkthrough, synthetic campaign, and virtual wafer runs inside an isolated sandbox state (Rule s1) so live measured cleanroom wafer records are never mutated. On this GitHub Pages build, a trained neural + analytical surrogate mirrors the full Python Brain directly in your browser.

1.banner_title: Step 1 Guide: Translating a Foundry Customer Spec (TSMC N2) into Machine-Checkable Acceptance Gates
1.what_happens: Every process development campaign starts with a customer's integration spec sheet — not an abstract ML loss function. In 2 nm / A16 Backside Power and 3D FinFET/GAA patterning, spin-on carbon (SOC) outgasses and shrinks during >= 400 °C anneals, so fabs demand high-temperature PECVD amorphous carbon (a-C:H:N) that fills both tight 110 nm vias (AR 9.1) and wide 225 nm trenches (AR 4.4) 1,000 nm deep with zero trapped seams, minimal top overburden (<= 85 nm) for single-step CMP, and high density (>= 1.80 g/cm³) for etch resistance.
1.how_to_use: Compare the two TSMC program presets below (or open 'Customize Spec Numbers Manually' to edit any threshold), inspect the 6 acceptance gates, and click 'Lock TSMC Spec & Continue to Step 2 →'.

deep_dives.q: Why are PH >= 985 nm and OB <= 85 nm in direct physical conflict?
deep_dives.a: Running deposition longer pushes more carbon into the trench to increase penetration depth (PH), but also piles thick blanket carbon onto the top planar field (Overburden, OB). Worse, if sticking probability β_eff is too high, the top mouth pinches shut early — so depositing longer ONLY grows top overburden while the buried keyhole void stays frozen inside!

deep_dives.q: Why does TSMC require XRR Film Density >= 1.80 g/cm³ and Zero Nodules?
deep_dives.a: After gap-fill and CMP planarization, the carbon plug acts as a hardmask during aggressive CF₄/O₂ plasma etching of underlying oxide/nitride. Low-density polymer-like carbon (< 1.78 g/cm³) etches away prematurely and loses critical dimension (CD), while even a single C₂ₙH⁻ dust nodule blocks etch locally and causes a killer bridge defect across metal lines.

2.banner_title: Step 2 Guide: Loading Screening Wafers & Diagnosing Why Every Baseline Recipe Fails (0/8 Pass)
2.what_happens: When a qualification starts, the team usually has an initial screening lot from legacy 13.56 MHz or exploratory 27.12 MHz single-step recipes. Instead of manually coloring Excel cells, Layer 1 ingests the screening lot (or your uploaded .csv/.json file), preserves nulls for unmeasured sensors, and grades every wafer line-by-line against Step 1's TSMC spec — immediately revealing three distinct physical failure walls.
2.how_to_use: Click 'Load 8-Wafer Preloaded Dataset' on the Recommended AMAT Producer Baseline Lot (or test the 6-wafer Dust Stress Lot / upload a CSV), then scan the red FAIL badges in the table to see why single-step tweaks hit a dead end.

deep_dives.q: What are the 3 failure walls revealed in the 8-wafer baseline lot?
deep_dives.a: (1) Legacy 13.56 MHz coupons (BL-01..04) suffer high sheath ion bombardment (~28 eV) that activates top-corner dangling bonds, pinching off 110 nm vias at 588–794 nm with 146–253 nm OB and corner cracks. (2) High pressure + low Ar (BL-02) triggers gas-phase C₂ₙH⁻ dust nodules. (3) Single-step 27.12 MHz (BL-06..08) reaches 964 nm fill at 118 nm OB, but cutting time (BL-07) starves fill to 815 nm, and adding excess NH₃ at 535 °C (BL-08) drops density to 1.74 g/cm³.

3.banner_title: Step 3 Guide: Versioned Knowledge Governance, IP Separation & Physics/Chemistry Priors
3.what_happens: Pure black-box ML needs hundreds of wafers because it starts ignorant of plasma sheaths, ballistic Knudsen transport, and chamber hardware limits. Layer 2 injects structured scientific and engineering priors into the Brain while enforcing strict IP governance across three tiers: (1) Public Peer-Reviewed Science (102 papers + 10 benchmark tables), (2) Proprietary AMAT Producer Chamber BKMs (AST-compiled rules PROP-AMAT-01..05), and (3) Customer Lot Metrology.
3.how_to_use: Try switching between KB v1.0 (Public Only), KB v2.0 (+ Chamber Hardware Guards), and KB v2.1 (Recommended Full Hybrid) to see how active rules change. Review the Chemistry & Physics incorporation cards and try the Configuration Paper Search below before continuing to Step 4A.

deep_dives.q: What actually changes inside the math when I switch KB v1.0 → KB v2.0 → KB v2.1?
deep_dives.a: KB v1.0 provides the Stage-1 CCP & DFT Bonding neural priors plus ballistic Knudsen physics, but leaves high-pressure dust and cyclic trim unguided. KB v2.0 activates proprietary hardware hazard penalties (PROP-AMAT-01..03) that zero out acquisition weight in dusty/arcing zones. KB v2.1 adds positive prior shifts and selectivity guidance for 27.12 MHz VHF + NH₃ passivation (PROP-AMAT-04) and cyclic Ar/NH₃ mouth trim (PROP-AMAT-05), cutting search waste by >60%.

deep_dives.q: How do Chemistry and Physics couple mathematically across Stages 1–4?
deep_dives.a: Gas-phase CCP physics sets electron density n_e and sheath ion energy E_i; gas/surface chemistry converts NH₃ + C₂H₂ radical ratios into volatile HCN scavenging and surface passivation coverage θ_pass(z), determining effective sticking β_eff; Knudsen ballistic transport maps β_eff into depth-resolved growth v_net(z) via Thiele modulus Φ; and Steinbrüchel ion-etch yield models cyclic Ar/NH₃ mouth shaving of top overburden.

4A.banner_title: Step 4A Guide: AI Gap Triage & Calling Coupled Multi-Scale Simulations In-Platform
4A.what_happens: Inspecting Step 2's data + Step 3's KB, the AI spots a critical blind spot: all 8 baseline wafers were single-step depositions (0% cyclic trim), so a purely data-driven model would have huge uncertainty in cyclic Dep–Etch–Dep (DED) space! Layer 3 bridges that gap before cutting cleanroom wafers by running coupled 3-scale simulations: Chamber CCP Plasma → 1D Ballistic Knudsen Feature Profile → 3D Atomistic a-C:H:N Network Relaxation.
4A.how_to_use: Click '⚡ Load Prebuilt 6-Run Multi-Scale Simulation Pack' to assimilate 6 benchmark simulations covering 13.56 vs. 27.12 MHz, 12%–24% cyclic trim, and high-NH₃ density dilution — then try tweaking the knobs on the right and clicking '▶ Run Live Multi-Scale Simulation' to execute a new coupled run on the spot!

deep_dives.q: How do the 3 simulation scales pass boundary conditions to each other?
deep_dives.a: (1) The CCP reactor model takes chamber knobs (RF, Power, Gap, P, Ar, C₂H₂, NH₃, T) and outputs ion energy E_i (eV), radical flux ratio Γ_(H+NHx)/Γ_C2Hx, and Knudsen number Kn. (2) The Feature-scale Knudsen solver uses those exact fluxes + cyclic trim fraction to integrate sidewall and bottom film evolution (PH₁₁₀, OB, keyhole void width). (3) The 3D Molecular engine (RDKit ETKDGv3 + MMFF94s, plus exportable LAMMPS ReaxFF C/H/N decks) relaxes a stoichiometric a-C:H:N cluster to predict sp²/sp³ fractions and bulk density ρ.

4B.banner_title: Step 4B Guide: Plain-English Process Synthesis & How to Read the Two Mechanism Figures
4B.what_happens: Before approving cleanroom wafers, a Principal PECVD Technologist and customer integration lead need an interpretable physical picture — not just a table of numbers. Step 4B synthesizes the calibrated kinetic parameters (θ̂), wafer residuals, and simulation pack into a clear mechanistic diagnosis plus two publication-grade visual figures.
4B.how_to_use: Read the 3 quantitative takeaways at top, then compare Panels A, B, and C in Figure 1 (left) and inspect where the red × baseline wafers, blue ◇ simulations, and green target box sit in Figure 2 (right).

deep_dives.q: How do I read Figure 1 (the 3 HAR Via Cross-Sections)?
deep_dives.a: Each column shows a 110 nm wide × 1000 nm deep SiO₂ via to scale, with the dashed amber line marking TSMC's 85 nm max planar overburden cap. In Panel A (13.56 MHz), high-energy ions create sticky upper sidewalls that bridge early and trap a large red keyhole void with 182 nm OB. In Panel B (27.12 MHz + NH₃, 0% trim), radicals bounce deep (964 nm) leaving a tiny 7.5 nm seam, but top OB (118 nm) still breaches the 85 nm line. In Panel C (+22% cyclic Ar/NH₃ trim), grazing-angle trim arrows shave the top collar and planar OB down to 63.8 nm while bottom-up growth fills 100% void-free.

deep_dives.q: How do I read Figure 2 (the 2D Operating Regime Map)?
deep_dives.a: The horizontal axis is NH₃/C₂H₂ flow ratio (controlling surface passivation vs. nitrogen incorporation) and the vertical axis is Cyclic Trim % (controlling top-mouth shaving). Left of N/C = 0.30 (pink) sticking is too high -> keyhole pinch-off. Below Trim = 14% (amber) planar overburden exceeds 85 nm. Right of N/C = 0.385 at low temperature (purple) excess -NH₂ softens density below 1.80 g/cm³. Notice all 8 baseline red × wafers sit along the bottom 0%-trim edge — completely outside the green TSMC Target Window!

5.banner_title: Step 5 Guide: Active Bayesian Optimization — Proposing the Fewest Wafers to Hit Spec
5.what_happens: Patterned 300 mm HAR test wafers and cross-section FIB-SEM slots are expensive (~$2,500–$4,000 per wafer including metrology and chamber time). Instead of a 27-wafer full-factorial DoE grid, Layer 3 evaluates thousands of candidate multi-step recipes using Constrained Expected Improvement (cEI) and selects a diverse 3-wafer cassette split with immutable UUID prediction logs.
5.how_to_use: Click '🎯 Run Bayesian Optimization' to generate the 3-wafer run-sheet. Inspect each wafer's assigned DoE role, predicted PH₁₁₀ ± σ, OB ± σ, density ρ, and P(Meets TSMC Spec), optionally export the .csv run-sheet for the chamber, then continue to Step 6.

deep_dives.q: Why does Bayesian Optimization propose 3 different roles instead of 3 nearly identical recipes?
deep_dives.a: Batch diversity (penalizing kernel correlation across the 3 slots) prevents wasting 3 wafers on the same unknown bias: Wafer #1 (Exploitation Anchor) targets the highest joint probability of passing TSMC's spec right now; Wafer #2 (High-Trim Low-OB Probe) pushes deeper into 24% cyclic trim to map the overburden floor; and Wafer #3 (Control / Boundary Guard) anchors RF sheath or thermal crosslinking sensitivity so the GP uncertainty collapses rapidly.

6.banner_title: Step 6 Guide: Cleanroom Metrology Return, Line-by-Line Grading & Prediction Audit
6.what_happens: After running the 3 proposed wafers in the Producer PECVD chamber and measuring cross-section CD-SEM, XRR density, inline OES, and AFM roughness, the results flow back into Layer 1. Every wafer is automatically graded against all 6 TSMC acceptance criteria, linked back to its pre-run UUID prediction to audit model accuracy, and assimilated to update θ̂ and GP posteriors.
6.how_to_use: Click '📥 Load & Auto-Grade Cleanroom Results (3 Wafers)' (or open the manual entry drawer to test your own numbers) and examine which spec lines turned green PASS vs. red FAIL.

deep_dives.q: Why doesn't Round 1 pass 100% immediately — and why is Round 1's 'near-miss' actually a huge win?
deep_dives.a: In real cleanroom development, jumping into a brand-new cyclic trim regime (0% -> 24% trim) often uncovers a secondary material trade-off! Round 1 solves the hardest geometric barriers immediately — TSMC-R1-W1 hits seamless 991.2 nm fill & 1.83 g/cm³ density (missing OB <= 85 nm by just 9.2 nm), while TSMC-R1-W2 hits 65.8 nm OB & 993.8 nm fill (missing ρ >= 1.80 g/cm³ by just 0.03 g/cm³ because high NH₃ at 544 °C left un-crosslinked -NH₂ groups). Bracketing both sides in 3 wafers gives the exact physical key needed to close qualification in Round 2!

7.banner_title: Step 7 Guide: Turning Round-1 Cleanroom Surprises into Versioned Institutional Knowledge (KB v2.2)
7.what_happens: When Round 1's TSMC-R1-W2 wafer comes back at ρ = 1.77 g/cm³ (< 1.80 spec), a conventional black-box optimizer only sees a scalar penalty on one data point. Here, the platform diagnoses the physical residual — aggressive NH₃ trim (>=18%) + high N/C (>0.38) below 555 °C retains terminal -NH₂ groups — and proposes an explicit, human-readable AST causal rule (PROP-TSMC-06) that upgrades your Knowledge Base from KB v2.1 to KB v2.2.
7.how_to_use: Read the Residual & Mechanism Diagnosis and the candidate AST rule expression, click '✓ Promote Rule PROP-TSMC-06 into Knowledge Base (Upgrade → KB v2.2)', then proceed to Step 8.

deep_dives.q: Why promote an explicit KB rule instead of relying purely on the Gaussian Process residual?
deep_dives.a: Two reasons: (1) Immediate global generalization — the rule steers Round 2 directly into T >= 560 °C + N/C ∈ [0.33, 0.37] across the entire recipe space instead of only within one local GP length-scale; and (2) Reusable institutional memory — when the next customer asks for a 95 nm HAR plug six months later, KB v2.2 already carries this verified Trim × Temperature crosslinking law!

8.banner_title: Step 8 Guide: Closing the Loop to 100% Spec Compliance & Cleanroom Recipe Sign-Off
8.what_happens: With KB v2.2 active and Round-1 metrology assimilated, repeating Steps 4–6 for Round 2 co-optimizes 27.12 MHz VHF plasma, N/C = 0.352 passivation, 22% cyclic Ar/NH₃ mouth trim, and 566 °C thermal de-amination. All 3 Round-2 wafers pass 100% of TSMC's criteria simultaneously — led by qualified winner TSMC-R2-W1 (PH₁₁₀ = 996.4 nm, PH₂₂₅ = 998.2 nm, OB = 63.8 nm, ρ = 1.84 g/cm³, AFM R_q = 1.18 nm, zero cracks/nodules).
8.how_to_use: If Round 2 hasn't run yet, click '⚡ Run Round 2 Loop (Steps 4–6) to Convergence Now' (or step through Round 2 manually). Once qualified, inspect the green TSMC Qualification Certificate, Trajectory Chart, export the .json sign-off package, or click '⚙ Inspect in 6-Tab Workbench' for deep diagnostics.

deep_dives.q: What is the bottom-line cleanroom ROI demonstrated by this 8-step campaign?
deep_dives.a: Qualification converged in just 2 active DoE rounds (6 optimization wafers + 8 baseline coupons = 14 patterned wafers total), compared with 8–10 manual trial-and-error rounds (45–60 wafers and 5–6 weeks of cross-team iteration) typical of dual-CD HAR gap-fill development — while leaving behind a versioned Knowledge Base (KB v2.2) and full UUID prediction-to-metrology audit trail.

har.definition: Feature depth divided by critical opening width (AR = Depth / CD). At AR >= 8:1 (e.g., 1000 nm deep / 110 nm wide = 9.1:1), reactive radicals collide dozens of times with upper sidewalls before reaching the floor.

ph_depth.definition: Depth from the top mold opening down to the shallowest void or seam inside the 110 nm tight feature or 225 nm wide feature. Seamless bottom-up plug fill requires PH >= 985 nm in a 1000 nm deep feature.

overburden.definition: Unwanted blanket carbon thickness deposited on top of the flat field between features. TSMC caps OB <= 85 nm so downstream CMP or plasma etch-back stays single-step without dishing.

keyhole_void.definition: A hollow teardrop cavity trapped inside the trench/via when upper sidewalls grow faster than the bottom and seal the throat early. Trapped voids outgas and burst during 400 °C anneal or plasma etch.

ccp.definition: Parallel-plate PECVD reactor architecture (e.g., Applied Materials Producer) where RF power across a heated showerhead-to-pedestal gap (400–500 mils) sustains the plasma.

vhf_27mhz.definition: Doubling RF frequency from 13.56 to 27.12 MHz increases electron density (n_e ~ f^2) for efficient NH₃/C₂H₂ dissociation while cutting capacitive sheath voltage V_sh and ion energy E_i (~29 eV -> ~11 eV), preventing top-corner overhang.

knudsen.definition: Ratio of gas mean free path (lambda ~ 8–14 um at 18 Torr) to feature width (CD = 110 nm). Because Kn ~ 70–130 >> 1, gas transport inside the feature is purely ballistic free-molecular bounce, not continuum fluid flow.

thiele.definition: Dimensionless competition between sidewall reaction loss and ballistic transport down the hole: Φ = AR * sqrt(1.5 * beta_eff). Seamless fill requires Φ < 0.85, which means lowering sticking probability beta_eff below ~0.008.

beta_eff.definition: Probability that a carbon growth radical sticks on a single wall collision. Unpassivated C₂H• has high β ~ 0.08 (sticks near the mouth); -H and -NH₂ surface passivation lowers β_eff below 0.007 so radicals bounce >100 times to the bottom.

hcn_scavenging.definition: Adding NH₃ supplies H• and NHₓ• radicals that cap surface dangling bonds with -H/-NH₂ and convert reactive C₂Hₓ oligomers into volatile HCN gas that pumps away harmlessly.

dust_nodule.definition: At high pressure (>20 Torr) and long gas residence time (low Ar dilution), C₂H⁻ anions polymerize in the plasma bulk into carbon nanoparticles that fall onto the wafer as killer nodule defects.

ded_trim.definition: Deposition–Etch–Deposition cycle where brief directional Ar⁺/NHₓ⁺ ion-assisted chemical etch selectively shaves the z < 120 nm top entrance collar and planar overburden without etching the shielded feature floor.

griffith_crack.definition: Elastic strain energy release rate G = sigma^2 * h_OB * (1 - nu) / E. When compressive stress sigma and planar overburden h_OB are both high (OB > 155 nm), G exceeds interfacial toughness G_c and the carbon film cracks.

film_density.definition: Bulk mass density measured by X-Ray Reflectivity. TSMC requires ρ >= 1.80 g/cm³ to guarantee pattern-transfer hardmask etch resistance in downstream CF₄/O₂ plasma.

afm_rq.definition: Root-mean-square top-surface height variation measured by inline Atomic Force Microscopy. Smooth sp²/sp³ carbon (R_q <= 1.6 nm) avoids lithography focus errors and post-CMP micro-scratches.

map_theta.definition: Maximum A Posteriori estimation of the 6 physical surface-kinetic constants (β_c0, k_pass, γ_rec, y_iece, ob_scale, crack_thresh) anchored to literature priors and updated every time cleanroom wafers arrive.

gp_discrepancy.definition: Non-parametric probabilistic model trained on the residual gap between calibrated physics and real wafer measurements, providing honest epistemic uncertainty (± σ) everywhere in recipe space.

constrained_ei.definition: Acquisition score cEI(x) = EI(x) * P(Meets All Spec Lines | x) * RulePrior(x) that balances exploiting high-probability sweet spots with exploring high-uncertainty regions that could unlock lower overburden.

reaxff.definition: Atomistic relaxation of amorphous C/H/N bonding networks (sp² rings, sp³ crosslinks, -NH₂/-C≡N terminations) predicting bulk density ρ, stress, and fluorine etch barriers before running wafers.

oes_actinometry.definition: Optical Emission Spectroscopy ratio dividing CN* radical emission (388.3 nm) by inert Ar* emission (750.4 nm) to track real-time HCN scavenging and nitrogen passivation inside the chamber without breaking vacuum.

rf_3w.definition: Ratio of 3rd-harmonic RF current to fundamental RF current at the matchbox. Non-linear sheath capacitance and trapped C₂ₙH⁻ dust clouds spike 3ω/1ω above 9.5%, providing an early warning before particle defects land.

dual_cd.definition: Real logic and memory dies place narrow vias (110 nm, AR 9.1) right next to wide trenches (225 nm, AR 4.4). A valid recipe must fill both simultaneously without voids in the narrow via or under-fill in the wide trench.

residence_time.definition: Average time gas molecules spend inside the active RF gap (τ_res ~ P * V_gap / Q_total). If τ_res exceeds ~42 ms in C₂H₂ plasma, negative C₂H⁻ ions have time to polymerize into killer dust nodules.

sp2_sp3.definition: Amorphous carbon hardmasks balance aromatic sp² rings (thermal stability), tetrahedral sp³ C-C crosslinks (mechanical stiffness & density), and C=N bridges. Terminal -NH₂/-CH₃ groups lower stress but dilute density if excessive.

etch_selectivity.definition: Carbon gap-fill plugs serve as sacrificial pattern-transfer masks during aggressive fluorocarbon oxide/nitride RIE. Dense carbon (ρ >= 1.80 g/cm³) raises the fluorine activation barrier so the mask erodes slowly.

loocv.definition: Honest small-data accuracy test: holds out 1 wafer at a time, re-runs both Bayesian MAP θ̂ calibration and GP fitting from scratch on the remaining N-1 wafers, and measures blind prediction error on the held-out wafer.

sandbox_s1.definition: Strict cleanroom data boundary: demo trials, virtual wafers, and synthetic DoE campaigns execute in an isolated sandbox brain so real measured customer wafer ledgers can never be overwritten or polluted.
